scientific_question: Does separating observation support from target evidence and nuisance risk prevent false biological absence and denominator contamination without treating all high-nuisance windows as unobservable?

policies.target_only: Uses target evidence only; low target evidence is treated as negative evidence regardless of nuisance/support.
policies.target_plus_nuisance: Uses target evidence and nuisance risks; low target evidence with low missed-event risk is treated as negative evidence, but no independent support gate exists.
policies.triad: Uses target evidence, nuisance risks, and independent observation support; unobservable windows are censored rather than counted as absence.

interpretation_rules: Do not collapse the primary metrics into one scalar winner.
A lower false-absence rate obtained only by censoring all high-nuisance windows is not sufficient evidence for the triad model.
The key V14 distinction is demonstrated only if low-nuisance unobservable windows can be censored while at least some high-nuisance observable windows remain denominator-eligible.
This development benchmark cannot establish field visit accuracy or calibrated detection probability.
locked_history_boundary: V7, V10, V11, V12, and V13 are not modified or reinterpreted by V14.
